thesis: MNCS-native execution should preserve runtime-relevant language meaning, authority, bounds, identity, and evidence instead of collapsing them into an opaque host process.
owns: runtime-specific VM artifact and instruction contract
artifact loading and runtime structural validation
runtime-local frames stacks regions heaps handles and transient state
runtime capability checks and effect mediation
runtime resource metering and bounded execution
execution-local scheduling required by VM semantics
structured traps failures refusals suspensions and completion
runtime execution identities traces transition digests and observations
runtime debug replay inspection and snapshot hooks
does_not_own: HIR SSA or compiler optimization policy
translation proof or compiler evidence authority
core_invariants: the VM executes frozen artifacts and does not redefine source-language meaning
the native VM is one backend target and does not invalidate direct WASM native accelerator or other backends
artifact callable runtime capability provider and resource identities remain explicit where required
the deterministic runtime core is reproducible under equal admitted inputs and configuration
external nondeterminism crosses explicit identifiable boundaries
capabilities are checked where authority is exercised
runtime bounds are enforced rather than retained only as metadata
structured runtime outcomes are not collapsed into generic process exits
runtime-local memory is distinct from semantic memory and durable storage
execution-local scheduling is distinct from workflow automation and distributed placement
runtime observations are structured machine data rather than log-only APIs
runtime observations are scoped evidence and are not automatically universal proof
host implementation details must not leak into defined VM semantics accidentally
capability enforcement is not by itself a claim of complete hostile-code sandboxing
the current research-bytecode interpreter is migration input rather than a permanent parallel runtime
the repository maintains one evolving canonical implementation unless a real external compatibility requirement exists

family_interfaces.mncs-language: source semantics compiler legality selected SSA lowering translation evidence and emission of identity-bound MNCS VM artifacts
family_interfaces.MNCS-Commons: cross-repository pressure exchange shared contracts identities and evidence coordination
family_interfaces.mncs-fabric: host device worker placement runtime packaging and run-environment orchestration
family_interfaces.mncs-actions: external action/provider contracts invoked only through explicit admitted capability boundaries
family_interfaces.mncs-automation: wall-clock and event-driven workflow scheduling outside execution-local VM scheduling
family_interfaces.mncs-memory: semantic memory retrieval and memory behavior exposed through explicit runtime interfaces
family_interfaces.mncs-store: durable persistence of VM artifacts runtime packages snapshots traces results and evidence
family_interfaces.mncs-test: structured invocation conformance comparison and bounded execution verification
family_interfaces.mncs-debug: diagnosis stepping inspection replay and debugging policy over structured VM runtime state
family_interfaces.mncs-doctor: runtime environment capability compatibility and health diagnosis
family_interfaces.mncs-forge: build experiment orchestration backend comparison and evidence campaigns using the VM as an execution target
family_interfaces.mncs-models: model structure that may be compiled for or dispatched through VM execution
family_interfaces.mncs-learn: learning and adaptation semantics that may use VM execution without transferring learning policy into the runtime
family_interfaces.mncs-rights-provenance: rights provenance lineage and identity policy associated with artifacts inputs providers and outputs
family_interfaces.mncs-crypto: cryptographic primitives hashing signatures and authenticated structures consumed through explicit contracts
family_interfaces.mncs-data: machine-native data contracts presented through VM runtime ABI and provider boundaries

migration_policy.current_source: mncs-language research-bytecode backend and bounded SSA interpreter
migration_policy.rule: Classify existing behavior into compiler semantics VM semantics integration contracts and disposable experiment scaffolding before moving code.
migration_policy.target: One canonical MNCS-native VM runtime, with obsolete duplicate language-owned runtime machinery removed after migration and verification.

determinism_policy.core: Defined VM semantics should be deterministic where language/runtime meaning allows it.
determinism_policy.external: Clocks randomness network devices users models remote providers and other external observations must cross explicit identifiable boundaries.
determinism_policy.host_leakage: Allocator addresses hash iteration order host thread timing and similar incidental behavior must not affect defined VM semantics unless explicitly specified.

evolution_policy: Maintain one canonical implementation and migrate known MNCS consumers forward. Do not create frozen v1/v2/legacy/next runtime trees without a real external compatibility obligation.
